papers.title: Identifying phase separation modulators mediated by the SARS-CoV-2 nucleocapsid protein using a structure-based drug discovery approach.
papers.abstract: As severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) continues to evolve through mutations and acquire resistance to existing antiviral agents, the persistence of post-pandemic infections remains a significant global health concern. To address these challenges, it is crucial to develop novel therapeutic agents that target previously unexplored viral or host mechanisms.
papers.summary: The paper applies a structure-based drug discovery approach to identify small molecules that modulate phase separation driven by the SARS-CoV-2 nucleocapsid protein, a mechanism not targeted by current antivirals. This offers a potential new therapeutic strategy against evolving SARS-CoV-2 variants.

papers.title: PROTAC-DB 4.0: an expanded knowledgebase of targeted protein degradation modalities with AI-powered knowledge discovery.
papers.abstract: Proteolysis-targeting chimeras (PROTACs) represent an emerging therapeutic modality that harnesses the ubiquitin-proteasome system to induce targeted protein degradation (TPD). Their event-driven and catalytic mechanisms provide new opportunities to target previously undruggable proteins. However, the rapid expansion of TPD technologies, including molecular glues (MGs) and X-functional targeting chimeras (XTACs), together with the increasing application of artificial intelligence (AI) in degrader design, highlights the need for comprehensive and continuously updated data resources. Here, we pr
papers.summary: PROTAC-DB 4.0 is an updated knowledgebase that expands coverage of targeted protein degradation modalities beyond classical PROTACs to include molecular glues and X-functional targeting chimeras (XTACs). It also integrates AI-powered knowledge discovery tools to help researchers mine the growing body of degrader data for design insights.

papers.title: Domain-Aware Enzyme Classification via Multiple Instance Learning.
papers.abstract: Accurate Enzyme Commission (EC) number prediction is fundamental to protein function annotation and metabolic pathway reconstruction. Recent methods based on protein language model embeddings or 3D structure have improved EC prediction, but important limitations remain. Whole-sequence embeddings can dilute local functional signals, such as catalytic residues and functional domains, whereas structure-based methods depend on accurate protein structures and are therefore difficult to apply broadly.
papers.summary: The paper introduces a domain-aware enzyme classification method that uses multiple instance learning to focus on local functional regions (e.g., catalytic residues and domains) rather than whole-sequence embeddings, avoiding reliance on 3D structures. This addresses the dilution of local functional signals in existing protein language model-based EC prediction approaches.

papers.title: ARIEL: an openly accessible database of experimental RNA-ligand binding affinities paired with 3D structures.
papers.abstract: RNA is an increasingly attractive target for small-molecule therapeutics, yet the rational design and computational modelling of RNA-binding small molecules are constrained by the scarcity of experimentally measured binding affinities linked to 3D structures. Here we present ARIEL (Affinity Resource for Interactions of RNA and Ligands), an openly accessible, manually curated database that pairs experimentally determined dissociation constants (Kd) of RNA-ligand complexes with the corresponding experimental structures. We screened 6954 RNA-containing structures from the Protein Data Bank, extra
papers.summary: ARIEL is a new, freely accessible database that manually curates experimentally measured binding affinities (Kd values) for RNA–small-molecule complexes and links each to its corresponding 3D experimental structure. By screening thousands of RNA-containing PDB entries, the resource fills a key gap for computational and rational design of RNA-targeting drugs, where affinity data tied to structures have been scarce.

papers.title: Harnessing engineered laccase and functional carrier materials for efficient dye degradation: From mechanism to application.
papers.abstract: Laccases are copper-containing oxidases that have been widely investigated for the decolorization and degradation of synthetic dyes, including azo, anthraquinone, triphenylmethane, indigo and thiazine dyes. However, their application in dye-containing wastewater remains constrained by enzyme instability under complex effluent conditions, limited oxidation of some recalcitrant or high-redox-potential dyes, mediator dependence, and poor recovery and reuse of free laccase. This review discusses recent progress in laccase-catalyzed dye degradation from a mechanism-to-engineering perspective, linki
papers.summary: This review examines recent progress in using laccase enzymes, combined with engineered variants and functional carrier materials, to degrade synthetic dyes in wastewater. It connects mechanistic understanding of laccase catalysis to practical engineering solutions that address enzyme instability, limited oxidation of recalcitrant dyes, mediator dependence, and poor enzyme recovery and reuse.

papers.title: Simulating Directed Evolution In Silico with an Iterative, Physics-Based Workflow.
papers.abstract: Directed evolution consistently delivers engineered enzymes that facilitate diverse biocatalytic transformations. Despite advances in automation and high-throughput workflows, our ability to rapidly engineer novel enzymes is limited by our inability to thoroughly sample the vast protein design space. Generative artificial intelligence (AI) methods have alleviated this challenge to some degree, due to their ability to propose mutations based on learned patterns from complex protein data sets. However, the hidden logic of these AI-based methods can complicate our ability to reveal and exploit fu
papers.summary: The paper presents an iterative, physics-based computational workflow that mimics directed evolution to engineer enzymes in silico, aiming to overcome the limited sampling of protein design space that constrains experimental directed evolution. Unlike generative AI approaches whose decision logic is opaque, this method uses physics-based scoring to propose and evaluate mutations across iterative cycles, potentially offering a more interpretable route to enzyme design.

papers.title: Discovery and Design of YTHDF2-Selective and Pan-YTHDF Inhibitors for m6A Binding by the YTH Aromatic Cage.
papers.abstract: Recognition of N6-methyl-adenosine (m6A) in the RNA sequences by the YT521-B homology domain-containing protein family paralogs 1-3 (YTHDF1-3) is a dominant layer of myriad cellular regulation. Dysregulated YTHDF paralog expression and activities have been reported in cancer, including glioblastoma multiforme (GBM) in which YTHDF2 has been identified as a druggable dependency. Guided by structure-based in silico screening, we identified structurally related small-molecule compound families of promising YTHDF inhibitor compounds. Following in vitro screening, two hits, DT11 and DT15, emerged an
papers.summary: The authors used structure-based virtual screening to identify small-molecule inhibitors that bind the m6A-binding aromatic cage of YTHDF proteins, yielding two hits (DT11 and DT15) with promising in vitro activity. These compounds include both YTHDF2-selective and pan-YTHDF inhibitors, providing chemical probes to dissect paralog-specific m6A reader functions and potential leads for cancers such as glioblastoma where YTHDF2 is a druggable dependency.

papers.title: Substrate recognition and stage-dependent transformation of aflatoxin B1 by mediator-free Bacillus laccase frL103.
papers.abstract: Enzyme-based mitigation of aflatoxin B1 (AFB1) is commonly evaluated by parent-toxin depletion. This study characterized the stage-dependent, mediator-free transformation of AFB1 by recombinant Bacillus laccase frL103 and assessed chemical, biological, and structural outcomes. UHPLC-HRMS profiling at 0, 30, and 60 h yielded 2846 filtered features and showed that the AFB1 response decreased to 23.8% and 14.8% of the initial value at 30 and 60 h, respectively. A feature at m/z 329.0660 increased at 30 h and declined to 17.7% of that response at 60 h; accurate mass and MS/MS fragmentation support
papers.summary: This study characterizes how a recombinant Bacillus laccase (frL103) degrades aflatoxin B1 without requiring a mediator, tracking the reaction over 60 hours. Using UHPLC-HRMS profiling, the authors show that AFB1 levels drop to ~24% and ~15% of initial at 30 and 60 hours, while a transient intermediate (m/z 329.0660) peaks at 30 hours and then declines, indicating stage-dependent transformation rather than simple depletion. The work highlights that parent-toxin disappearance alone is an incomplete measure of detoxification and provides structural evidence for intermediate products.

papers.title: Bisphenol A induces ACSL4-associated ferro-aging-like urothelial injury: Implications for Hunner-type interstitial cystitis.
papers.abstract: Hunner-type interstitial cystitis (HIC) is an inflammatory subtype of interstitial cystitis/bladder pain syndrome marked by persistent urothelial injury and bladder dysfunction. Bisphenol A (BPA) can disturb redox and inflammatory homeostasis, but its relevance to HIC-associated urothelial vulnerability remains unclear. This study examined whether acyl-CoA synthetase long-chain family member 4 (ACSL4) contributes to BPA-associated ferro-aging-like urothelial injury. Among non-pregnant adult women, higher creatinine-corrected urinary BPA was associated with a phenotype predominantly characteriz
papers.summary: This study links exposure to the environmental contaminant bisphenol A (BPA) to urothelial injury resembling ferroptosis and cellular aging, mediated by the lipid-metabolism enzyme ACSL4. In a human cohort, higher urinary BPA was associated with a phenotype consistent with this injury pattern, and mechanistic work implicates ACSL4 in the process. The findings suggest BPA exposure may contribute to Hunner-type interstitial cystitis, a painful bladder condition marked by persistent urothelial damage.

papers.title: On the limits of marginal protein folding stability: methodological goals and drawbacks.
papers.abstract: Why do proteins remain at the edge of stability rather than evolving toward maximal thermodynamic robustness? Can we trust the computational methods that inform about when and how stability falls off that edge? Marginal stability, the confinement of protein folding free energies to a window of approximately 5-15 kcal/mol, is broadly observed in biophysics, and its mechanistic causes, involving evolutionary and biophysical properties, remain under debate and require accurate predictions. In this regard, protein folding stability is currently predicted using both traditional structure-based homo
papers.summary: This paper critically examines why proteins evolve to be only marginally stable (folding free energies of ~5–15 kcal/mol) rather than maximally stable, and evaluates the reliability of computational methods used to predict folding stability. It discusses the evolutionary and biophysical explanations for marginal stability and highlights methodological limitations and drawbacks in current structure-based prediction approaches.

papers.title: Comparative Analysis of Relative Ligand Binding Free Energy Simulation Methods: Amber-TI, GROMACS-NETI, OpenMM-FEP, and BLaDE-MSLD.
papers.abstract: Structure-based drug design has become increasingly important in the pharmaceutical industry for accelerating the discovery of effective drug candidates. In particular, ligand binding free energy serves as a critical metric for predicting drug efficacy during the key stages of hit discovery and lead optimization. Continuous progress has been made in the prediction of ligand binding free energies, but direct comparisons of different methods using the same force field remain challenging due to their unique implementations in different simulation engines. In this study, we present a direct compar
papers.journal: Journal of chemical theory and computation
papers.summary: This study directly compares four relative ligand binding free energy simulation methods—Amber-TI, GROMACS-NETI, OpenMM-FEP, and BLaDE-MSLD—using the same force field to control for implementation differences across simulation engines. The comparison provides a controlled benchmark of accuracy and performance for these widely used free energy calculation approaches in structure-based drug design.

papers.title: SynBioFooDB: a comprehensive resource for synthetic biology-driven food biomanufacturing.
papers.abstract: Enabled by synthetic biology and metabolic engineering, microbial biomanufacturing is reshaping the production of food-related compounds by offering sustainable alternatives to resource-intensive extraction and conventional chemical synthesis. However, information linking food-related compounds to biosynthetic pathways and microbial biomanufacturing evidence remains fragmented across the literature and poorly represented in existing food-oriented resources, hindering cross-study comparison, evidence synthesis, and rational design of microbial production systems. Here, we present SynBioFooDB (h
papers.summary: SynBioFooDB is a new database that links food-related compounds to their biosynthetic pathways and microbial biomanufacturing evidence, addressing the fragmentation of this information across literature and existing food resources. It aims to enable cross-study comparison, evidence synthesis, and rational design of microbial production systems for food compounds.

papers.title: DockBind: A Quality-Controlled Data Set of Modeled Protein-Ligand Complexes Associated with Affinity Data.
papers.abstract: Ligand-protein interaction prediction is essential for structure-based drug discovery, but further development of machine-learning scoring functions is limited by a lack of high-quality training data sets. Here, we present DockBind, a curated data set of modeled protein-ligand complexes paired with experimental binding affinity data, generated through a quality-controlled docking workflow. This workflow was developed based on an expanded docking benchmark, where we systematically evaluated free and template-based docking methods as well as ligand similarity and maximum common substructure (MCS
papers.journal: Journal of chemical information and modeling
papers.summary: DockBind is a curated dataset of modeled protein-ligand complexes paired with experimental binding affinity data, built through a quality-controlled docking workflow. The authors systematically benchmarked free and template-based docking methods, along with ligand similarity and maximum common substructure approaches, to establish quality controls. This resource aims to address the shortage of high-quality training data that limits development of machine-learning scoring functions for structure-based drug discovery.

papers.title: A piperamide natural compound is compatible with an inactive DFG-out conformation of vascular endothelial growth factor receptor-2: In silico and in vitro model study.
papers.abstract: Vascular endothelial growth factor receptor-2 (VEGFR2) is a well-known key regulator of angiogenic cancers. In a structure-based virtual screening of Indonesian natural compounds, dehydropipernonaline (DPN), a piperamide from Piper species, emerged as a promising VEGFR2-binding candidate. However, its inhibitory activity against VEGFR2 has not been experimentally validated. This study combined molecular simulations and cellular assays to investigate the potential interaction between DPN and VEGFR2. Molecular docking predicted that DPN occupies the regulatory domain pocket (RDP) spanning the ca
papers.summary: This study used structure-based virtual screening to identify dehydropipernonaline (DPN), a piperamide natural compound, as a candidate VEGFR2 binder that occupies the regulatory domain pocket and is compatible with an inactive DFG-out conformation of the kinase. Molecular docking and simulations were combined with cellular assays to validate the predicted interaction and inhibitory activity against VEGFR2, a key regulator of angiogenic cancers.

papers.title: In-silico transcriptomic characterization analysis identifies SMAD5, USP2, and CUL4A as key biomarkers and therapeutic targets in colorectal cancer.
papers.abstract: Colorectal cancer (CRC) is a molecularly heterogeneous malignancy requiring reproducible biomarkers and structurally tractable therapeutic targets. We applied an integrated transcriptomic, network, virtual-screening, docking, ADMET, and molecular-dynamics (MD) workflow using GSE8671, GSE14333, and GSE89076. Differential expression analysis (adjusted p < 0.05, |log2FC= ≥ 1) identified 2092 upregulated/9130 downregulated genes in GSE8671, 926/945 in GSE14333, and 2317/1456 in GSE89076. Cross-dataset concordance was highest between GSE8671 and GSE89076 (r = 0.70), with 1040 shared upregulated and
papers.summary: This study integrates transcriptomic datasets from three colorectal cancer cohorts to identify differentially expressed genes, then uses network analysis and virtual screening to nominate SMAD5, USP2, and CUL4A as candidate biomarkers and druggable targets. The work is entirely computational, with no experimental validation, so the biomarkers remain hypotheses requiring wet-lab confirmation.

papers.title: Thermophysically Guided Design of Spray-Dried Lactiplantibacillus plantarum Microcapsules with Improved Thermal Stability.
papers.abstract: Spray drying and gastrointestinal transit can cause substantial losses in probiotic viability, limiting effective delivery in food applications. This study developed a thermophysically guided framework for the rational design of Lactiplantibacillus plantarum microcapsules in three sequential stages. First, Kissinger kinetic analysis of eleven biopolymer candidates (Ea: 95.4-198.4 kJ/mol) combined with pH-dependent solubility profiling provided an empirical screening criterion for the preselection of coating materials; the activation energies are apparent values associated with a composite endo
papers.summary: This study presents a three-stage framework for designing spray-dried Lactiplantibacillus plantarum microcapsules, using Kissinger kinetic analysis of eleven biopolymer candidates (activation energies 95.4–198.4 kJ/mol) plus pH-dependent solubility profiling to preselect coating materials. The approach aims to reduce viability losses during spray drying and gastrointestinal transit, improving probiotic delivery in foods.

papers.title: Adhesives Inspired by Marine Organisms: Multifunctional Design and Application for Complex Wet/Underwater Environments.
papers.abstract: Achieving strong adhesion in humid or underwater environments is a long-term challenge in materials science. Water molecules form a hydration layer on the substrate surface, blocking effective contact between the adhesive and the interface, leading to the failure of traditional adhesives. The wet adhesion strength of viscoelastic materials is due to the synergistic effect of interfacial chemical bonds and multiscale energy dissipation, but water environment can seriously interfere with this mechanism. In nature, mussels, barnacles, and sandcastle worms have evolved unique wet adhesion strategi
papers.summary: This review surveys how marine organisms such as mussels, barnacles, and sandcastle worms achieve strong wet and underwater adhesion despite the hydration layer that defeats conventional adhesives. It discusses the synergistic mechanisms—interfacial chemical bonding plus multiscale energy dissipation—that underlie biological wet adhesion and how these inspire multifunctional adhesive designs for complex wet environments. The paper is a materials-science synthesis rather than a primary experimental or bioinformatics study.

papers.title: Microbial Rhodopsins: Structural-Functional Mechanisms and the Design of Optogenetic Silencing Tools-With Emphasis on Halorubrum Archaeorhodopsins.
papers.abstract: Microbial rhodopsins are light-sensitive membrane proteins that use retinal as a covalent chromophore and adopt a seven-transmembrane α-helical fold. They are widely distributed across archaea, bacteria, algae, and fungi and mediate diverse functions, including light-driven ion transport, light-gated ion conduction, and photosensory signaling. Since the discovery of bacteriorhodopsin in 1971, the microbial rhodopsin family has expanded continuously, and channelrhodopsin-based optogenetics has revolutionized neuroscience by enabling millisecond-scale optical control of neuronal activity. Howeve
papers.summary: This review examines the structural and functional mechanisms of microbial rhodopsins—seven-transmembrane retinal-binding proteins found across archaea, bacteria, algae, and fungi—that mediate light-driven ion transport, light-gated conduction, and photosensory signaling. It traces the field from bacteriorhodopsin's discovery to channelrhodopsin-based optogenetics, with particular emphasis on Halorubrum archaeorhodopsins as a basis for designing optogenetic silencing tools. The paper synthesizes how structural features translate into function to guide engineering of improved inhibitory optogenetic actuators.

papers.title: Rational Design of Molecularly Imprinted Nanozymes for Selective Degradation of Poly(bisphenol A carbonate) (BPA-PC).
papers.abstract: Poly(bisphenol A carbonate) (BPA-PC) is an engineering thermoplastic whose recycling is hindered by its Code-7 classification and environmental BPA leaching. Here, we report water-soluble molecularly imprinted nanozymes for the selective depolymerization of BPA-PC under mild alkaline conditions. Synthesized within cross-linked surfactant micelles, the optimized nanozyme combines shape-complementary BPA-matched pockets with surface basicity, achieving a 72-fold rate enhancement over porcine pancreatic lipase. Fluorescence titrations with a soluble dansyl-labeled BPA-PC dimer confirm strong subs
papers.summary: The authors designed water-soluble molecularly imprinted nanozymes that selectively depolymerize poly(bisphenol A carbonate) under mild alkaline conditions, achieving a 72-fold rate enhancement over porcine pancreatic lipase. The nanozymes combine shape-complementary BPA-matched binding pockets with surface basicity, offering a potential route to recycling this hard-to-recycle plastic and reducing environmental BPA leaching.

papers.title: A Dipeptide Module Substitution-Based Strategy for the Modification and Evaluation of ACE Inhibitory Peptides.
papers.abstract: Food-derived angiotensin-converting enzyme (ACE) inhibitory peptide LYPVK exhibits promising potential for application as an important ingredient with a potential antihypertensive effect in functional foods. However, the structure-activity relationship and the rational design strategy for peptide modification remain insufficiently understood. To address this, dipeptide module substitution was employed to modify and investigate the mechanism of this food-derived ACE inhibitory peptide, providing an insight into the structure-activity relationship. Through integration of molecular docking and ac
papers.summary: The study uses a dipeptide module substitution strategy to modify the food-derived ACE inhibitory peptide LYPVK, aiming to clarify its structure-activity relationship and enable rational design of improved antihypertensive peptides. By combining molecular docking with activity evaluation, the authors identify which dipeptide modules are critical for ACE inhibition and show that targeted substitution can modulate potency. This provides a practical framework for engineering food-derived ACE inhibitory peptides.

papers.title: Food-Derived Umami Peptides: Linking Candidate Discovery, Experimental Validation, and Food Applications.
papers.abstract: Alternative proteins and cultivated meat increase the need for flavour strategies that maintain savoury quality with less reliance on salt and conventional seasonings. Food-derived umami peptides are promising candidates, but their practical value depends on evidence beyond sequence prediction. With advances in virtual digestion, peptidomics, and AI-assisted approaches, discovery is expanding from sensory-guided preparation toward candidate-library construction and data-driven prioritization. This review compares food-protein resources and experimental and sequence-based discovery routes, and
papers.summary: This review examines how food-derived umami peptides are discovered and validated, comparing traditional sensory-guided approaches with newer computational strategies such as virtual digestion, peptidomics, and AI-assisted candidate prioritization. It highlights that the practical value of these peptides depends on experimental evidence beyond sequence prediction, and surveys food-protein resources and discovery routes relevant to reducing salt and conventional seasoning reliance in alternative proteins and cultivated meat.

papers.title: Forecasting and Dynamics of Huntington's disease: A Machine Learning approach for Fractional-Order Mathematical Model.
papers.abstract: Huntington's disease (HD) is an autosomal dominant neurodegenerative disorder caused by expansion of CAG repeats in the HTT gene, leading to accumulation of mutant huntingtin and progressive neuronal dysfunction, particularly in vulnerable brain regions such as the striatum. Although length of CAG repeats is a major determinant of the risk of disease, it does not account for all the variance in age of onset, rate of progression or region of neurodegeneration. The aim of this work was to construct a fractional-order mathematical model to investigate the potential role of pure, interrupted and m
papers.summary: This paper builds a fractional-order mathematical model of Huntington's disease progression and couples it with machine learning to forecast disease dynamics. The model incorporates the effects of pure versus interrupted CAG repeat tracts, aiming to explain variability in age of onset and progression beyond repeat length alone. It represents a modeling and forecasting contribution rather than an experimental or clinical validation study.

papers.title: NADPH-specific meso-diaminopimelate dehydrogenase from the archaeon Pyrococcus sp. stereoselectively aminates α-keto acids using NADH.
papers.abstract: Enzymatic asymmetric D-amination of carbonyl compounds and keto acids is of great interest in biotechnology. Stable D-stereoselective NAD-dependent dehydrogenases are required for the synthesis of D-amino acids from α-keto acids, because they can use ammonium ion as the amino group donor and allow high product yield via coenzyme recycling. However, these enzymes are rare in nature. Here, we describe the first archaeal meso-diaminopimelate dehydrogenase from Pyrococcus sp. (PyrDAPDH). The enzyme is active with either NADP(H) or NAD(H) and catalyzes reductive amination of various α-keto acids an
papers.summary: The authors identify and characterize the first meso-diaminopimelate dehydrogenase from a Pyrococcus archaeon (PyrDAPDH), which can use either NADPH or NADH to stereoselectively aminate α-keto acids into D-amino acids. This expands the limited toolkit of stable, D-stereoselective dehydrogenases useful for biocatalytic production of D-amino acids with coenzyme recycling.

papers.title: Identification of small-molecule inhibitors of the SARS-CoV-2 RBD-ACE2 interaction by structure- and affinity-based screening.
papers.abstract: The receptor-binding domain (RBD) of the severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) spike protein mediates viral entry through its interaction with angiotensin-converting enzyme 2 (ACE2), making it an attractive target for antiviral intervention. However, the broad and relatively shallow ACE2-binding interface presents a challenge for small-molecule inhibitor discovery. In this study, we explored conserved regions outside the ACE2-binding interface as potential druggable sites for small-molecule inhibitors targeting the SARS-CoV-2 RBD. Structure-based virtual screening was pe
papers.summary: The authors used structure-based virtual screening combined with affinity-based methods to search for small molecules that inhibit the SARS-CoV-2 spike RBD–ACE2 interaction, focusing on conserved regions outside the shallow ACE2-binding interface as alternative druggable sites. This offers a potential route to antiviral compounds targeting viral entry, though the work appears to be at the screening/identification stage.

papers.title: Design, synthesis, and docking analysis of benzene sulfonamide-[1,4]benzoxazepine hybrids as acetylcholinesterase and butyrylcholinesterase inhibitors.
papers.abstract: A series of novel hybrid [1,4]benzoxazepine-based sulfonamide derivatives 9-12a-j were synthesized and evaluated for their inhibitory activity against acetylcholinesterase (AChE) and butyrylcholinesterase (BChE). Compounds 9a and 9b exhibited potent dual cholinesterase inhibition, with IC50 values of 9.04 and 8.61 µM against AChE and 3.08 and 4.64 µM against BChE, respectively. Compound 12j emerged as the most potent BChE inhibitor of the series (IC50 = 1.06 ± 0.11 µM), displaying pronounced BChE preference (SI = 10.37), whereas 9d showed the highest BChE selectivity (BChE IC50 = 4.18 ± 0.56 µ
papers.summary: The authors synthesized a series of hybrid [1,4]benzoxazepine-sulfonamide compounds and tested them as inhibitors of acetylcholinesterase (AChE) and butyrylcholinesterase (BChE), enzymes targeted in Alzheimer's disease. Several compounds showed micromolar dual inhibition, with compound 12j being the most potent BChE inhibitor (IC50 = 1.06 µM) and showing selectivity for BChE over AChE. Docking analysis was used to rationalize binding. This is an early-stage medicinal chemistry study with in vitro data only.

papers.title: Structural basis of phospholipid sensing nuclear receptor LRH-1 recognition by carboxylic acid bioisosteres reveals an alternative ligand interaction site.
papers.abstract: Liver receptor homolog-1 (LRH-1; NR5A2) is a phospholipid-sensing nuclear receptor that regulates metabolic and steroidogenic pathways in the liver, intestine, and pancreas. Previously, we showed that small-molecule LRH-1 agonists with carboxylic acid "tails" mimic endogenous phospholipid contacts at the mouth of the ligand-binding pocket, enhancing receptor activation. To improve metabolic stability while preserving these key interactions, we designed a series of agonists in which the carboxylate was replaced with bioisosteric polar groups. Substituting a tetrazole for the carboxylate in a le
papers.summary: The authors designed LRH-1 agonists in which the carboxylate group was replaced with bioisosteric polar groups (e.g., tetrazole) to improve metabolic stability while preserving key phospholipid-mimicking contacts. Structural analysis revealed that these bioisosteres engage an alternative ligand interaction site at the mouth of the ligand-binding pocket, providing a structural basis for how LRH-1 senses phospholipids and how agonists can be optimized.

papers.title: Discovery of potential ALK inhibitors from Glycosmis phytochemicals via integrated machine learning and umbrella sampling approaches.
papers.abstract: Anaplastic lymphoma kinase (ALK) is a key therapeutic target for various cancers because of its central role in tumor growth and survival signaling. This study employed an integrated computational workflow combining machine learning (ML), molecular docking, molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, umbrella sampling (US), and toxicity prediction to identify potential ALK inhibitors from 307 phytochemicals of the Glycosmis genus. A previously validated CatBoost regression model predicted binding free energies, leading to the selection of 26 compounds with ΔG ML < -11 kcal mol-1. Molecular docking id
papers.summary: This study used a computational pipeline combining machine learning, molecular docking, molecular dynamics, and umbrella sampling to screen 307 phytochemicals from the Glycosmis genus for potential ALK inhibitors. A CatBoost model predicted binding free energies, narrowing the set to 26 compounds with strong predicted affinity, which were then evaluated by docking and simulation. The work identifies candidate natural-product ALK inhibitors for further experimental validation.

papers.title: Design principles for natural SGLT2 modulators from multi-scale computation.
papers.abstract: Human sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 (hSGLT2) is a membrane-embedded renal transporter and an established therapeutic target for type 2 diabetes. Hyperoside, myricetin, cyanidin-3-O-glucoside and isoliquiritigenin were investigated as a chemically diverse panel of natural scaffolds using a multi-scale computational workflow combining redocking-validated molecular docking, reconstruction of an unresolved transporter segment, molecular dynamics (MD) in an explicit POPC bilayer, molecular mechanics/Poisson-Boltzmann surface area (MM/PBSA) calculations, principal component and free-energy landscap
papers.summary: This study uses a multi-scale computational pipeline—docking, molecular dynamics in a lipid bilayer, MM/PBSA, and free-energy landscape analysis—to characterize how four natural compounds (hyperoside, myricetin, cyanidin-3-O-glucoside, isoliquiritigenin) bind and modulate the human SGLT2 transporter. The work derives design principles for natural SGLT2 modulators and highlights how chemically diverse scaffolds interact with the transporter's binding site. It is a computational, structure-based exploration rather than experimental validation.

papers.title: Design, click synthesis, and biological evaluation of novel uracil-1,2,3-triazole hybrids as dual EGFR/CDK1 inhibitors: antiproliferative activity, mechanistic insights, and in silico studies.
papers.abstract: A novel series of uracil-1,2,3-triazole hybrids was designed, synthesized, and evaluated as dual EGFR/CDK1 inhibitors to target cancer cell proliferation and survival. Synthesis was initiated via the nucleophilic substitution of 2-chloro-N-(1,3-dimethyl-2,6-dioxo-pyrimidin-4-yl)acetamide (3) with sodium azide, yielding the key intermediate 4. Subsequent copper-catalyzed azide-alkyne cycloadditions (CuAAC) with various terminal alkynes and 1,3-dicarbonyls afforded the target triazole analogues 6a,b, 8a-c, and 10b,c. In vitro antiproliferative screening against a panel of four human cancer cell
papers.summary: The authors designed and synthesized a series of uracil-1,2,3-triazole hybrid compounds using click chemistry and tested them as dual inhibitors of EGFR and CDK1, two kinases important for cancer cell growth and division. The compounds showed antiproliferative activity against several human cancer cell lines, and the authors used computational (in silico) docking studies to rationalize how the hybrids bind both targets. This is an early-stage medicinal chemistry effort identifying a new scaffold for dual-target cancer therapy.

papers.title: Whole-proteome structure/function prediction in uropathogenic E. coli reveals previously missed host-microbe and microbe-phage interaction pathways.
papers.abstract: The rapid advancement of high-throughput sequencing technologies has vastly increased the number of known protein sequences, but the experimental characterization of their structures and functions lags behind. This gap in knowledge impedes our understanding of biological mechanisms of these proteins, hinders the interpretation of high-throughput experiments, and exposes a significant challenge in modern biology: deducing the structural and functional information of proteins based on their sequences. Most computational approaches rely on homology with well-annotated proteins, yet many proteins
papers.summary: The authors applied whole-proteome structure and function prediction to uropathogenic E. coli, going beyond homology-based annotation to uncover previously missed host-microbe and microbe-phage interaction pathways. This demonstrates how structure-informed proteome-scale analysis can reveal functional roles for uncharacterized proteins and improve interpretation of high-throughput data.

papers.title: Tomatidine derivatives suppress Dengue virus infection through entry and post-entry inhibition.
papers.abstract: Dengue is a rapidly spreading disease transmitted by mosquitoes and is caused by the Dengue virus (DENV), affecting approximately 390 million individuals globally. Approved vaccines for use have limited efficacy, and there are no approved antivirals. Tomatidine, a steroidal alkaloid obtained from Solanum species, has demonstrated broad-spectrum antiviral properties, leading to the investigation of its derivatives for their anti-DENV activity. In the current study, the anti-DENV potential of tomatidine and 11 such derivatives was assessed using a combination of in vitro and in silico approaches
papers.summary: This study tested tomatidine, a steroidal alkaloid from Solanum plants, and 11 of its derivatives for activity against Dengue virus using in vitro and computational approaches. Several derivatives suppressed DENV infection by blocking both viral entry and post-entry steps, suggesting these compounds could be developed as antiviral leads. Given the lack of approved DENV antivirals, this work identifies promising candidates for further drug development.

papers.title: EvoSeq-ML: Advancing Data-Centric Machine Learning with Evolutionary-Informed Protein Sequence Representation and Generation.
papers.abstract: From protein structure prediction to novel protein generation, challenging protein engineering tasks have been made possible by advancements in machine learning (ML). While largely driven by ML architecture refinements, these advancements in ML-based protein engineering campaigns have left the impact of data curation underexplored. In light of the growing wealth of labeled sequence data, data-centric advances (e.g. prioritizing improvements in ML protein engineering tools through the curation of high-quality, domain-specific training data) are increasingly preferred over model-centric advancem
papers.summary: EvoSeq-ML argues that data curation, not just model architecture, drives progress in ML-based protein engineering. The authors introduce an evolutionary-informed approach to representing and generating protein sequences, prioritizing high-quality, domain-specific training data over model refinements. This data-centric framework aims to improve tasks like protein structure prediction and novel protein design.

papers.title: Enterovirus 2C Protein Drug Design, Assay Development, and Drug Resistance Studies.
papers.abstract: In this Account, we describe our efforts to establish enteroviral 2C as a tractable target for antiviral drug discovery by integrating medicinal chemistry, molecular pharmacology, resistance profiling, structural modeling, and assay development. Rather than relying solely on conventional phenotypic high-throughput screening, our initial studies focused on the rational optimization of reported 2C inhibitors identified from a drug-repurposing campaign. This strategy led to quinoline-based antivirals with substantially improved potency and selectivity against enterovirus D68 (EV-D68), providing e
papers.summary: This account describes a rational drug-discovery campaign targeting the enterovirus 2C protein, starting from repurposed hits and optimizing them into quinoline-based antivirals with improved potency and selectivity against EV-D68. The work integrates medicinal chemistry, resistance profiling, structural modeling, and assay development to validate 2C as a tractable antiviral target.

papers.title: From structure prediction to ligand-target recognition: expanding the reach of AlphaFold in natural product research.
papers.abstract: Natural products constitute a structurally diverse reservoir of bioactive molecules and remain an important source of lead compounds for drug discovery. However, the limited availability of structural information on pharmacological targets and biomolecular interactions continues to hinder mechanism elucidation and structure-guided optimization, particularly for complex natural products such as bioactive peptides, proteinaceous natural products, and natural molecular glues. Recent advances in AlphaFold have transformed structural biology by enabling high-confidence prediction of protein structu
papers.summary: This review discusses how AlphaFold's protein structure prediction capabilities can be extended to ligand-target recognition in natural product research. It highlights that while AlphaFold has transformed structural biology, challenges remain in elucidating mechanisms and optimizing complex natural products like bioactive peptides and molecular glues due to limited structural data on targets and interactions.

papers.title: Atomistic insights into the migration and diffusion behavior of crosslinking byproducts in polyethylene networks.
papers.abstract: The accumulation of crosslinking byproducts, such as cumyl alcohol and acetophenone, in polyethylene (PE) insulation accelerates the degradation of high-voltage direct current (HVDC) cables through space charge formation and electrical tree propagation. Since conventional degassing processes cannot entirely eliminate these crosslinking byproducts, characterizing their residual dynamic behavior is of paramount importance. This work presents a comprehensive molecular dynamics (MD) simulation study to quantify the diffusion kinetics of these byproducts within the PE network. By systematically var
papers.summary: This study uses molecular dynamics simulations to quantify how crosslinking byproducts (cumyl alcohol and acetophenone) migrate and diffuse through polyethylene networks used in high-voltage cable insulation. The authors systematically vary network parameters to characterize diffusion kinetics, providing atomistic insight into why these residual byproducts are hard to remove by degassing and how they contribute to insulation degradation.

papers.title: Unrevealed oligoresveratrols from Shorea parvifolia root bark as xanthine oxidase inhibitors: isolation, in vitro bioassay, quantum studies and structure-based computational profiling.
papers.abstract: Resveratrol oligomers from Shorea species possess diverse biological activities, but the structural determinants governing their inhibition of xanthine oxidase (XO) remain poorly understood. This study investigated oligoresveratrols isolated from the root bark of Shorea parvifolia and examined how their structures relate to XO inhibitory potential. Five oligoresveratrols were isolated and structurally characterized by spectroscopic analysis. We evaluated their XO inhibitory activities, followed by pharmacokinetic and drug-likeness predictions, DFT calculations, molecular docking, and molecular
papers.summary: This study isolated five resveratrol oligomers from Shorea parvifolia root bark and tested their ability to inhibit xanthine oxidase, an enzyme target for gout treatment. The authors combined in vitro bioassays with computational approaches (DFT calculations, molecular docking, and pharmacokinetic predictions) to explore how structural features of these compounds relate to inhibitory activity. The work provides initial structure-activity insights for plant-derived oligoresveratrols as potential xanthine oxidase inhibitors.

papers.title: Integrated experimental and computational study of a novel indenonaphthodiazepine[5.3.3]propellane as a potential inhibitor of Mcl-1.
papers.abstract: Myeloid cell leukemia-1 (Mcl-1) is a key anti-apoptotic protein that drives resistance to chemotherapy, making it a critical oncology target. In this study, we synthesized a new indenonaphthodiazepine[5.3.3]propellane via a one-pot multicomponent reaction and characterized its structure by FT-IR, 1H-NMR, 13C-NMR, and mass spectrometry. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations at the B3LYP/6-31G (d) level were carried out to study its electronic features and reactive centers. In molecular docking against Mcl-1, the propellane derivative showed a binding score of -5.678 kcal mol-1, outperfor
papers.summary: The authors synthesized a novel indenonaphthodiazepine[5.3.3]propellane compound via a one-pot multicomponent reaction and characterized it spectroscopically. DFT calculations and molecular docking against the anti-apoptotic protein Mcl-1 suggested favorable binding (-5.678 kcal/mol), nominating it as a potential oncology drug lead. The work is preliminary, relying on computational docking without experimental validation of Mcl-1 inhibition.

papers.title: InterPro: the protein sequence classification resource in 2027.
papers.abstract: InterPro (https://www.ebi.ac.uk/interpro) is a freely accessible resource for the classification of protein sequences. It integrates predictive models, known as signatures, from multiple member databases to classify sequences into families and to predict the presence of domains and functionally important sites. The InterPro database provides annotations for hundreds of millions of sequences, ensuring extensive coverage of UniProtKB, the standard repository of protein sequences, and includes mapping to several other major resources, such as Gene Ontology, the Protein Data Bank in Europe (PDBe),
papers.summary: InterPro is a freely accessible database that classifies protein sequences by integrating predictive models (signatures) from multiple member databases to assign proteins to families and identify domains and functional sites. The 2027 update provides annotations for hundreds of millions of sequences, achieving extensive coverage of UniProtKB and linking to resources such as Gene Ontology and PDBe. This makes it a central reference for protein function annotation across the life sciences.

papers.title: A split nozzle and two-protein chain-like fibers define the tail architecture of Pseudomonas aeruginosa podophage A1002.
papers.abstract: Phage therapy offers unique advantages against antibiotic-resistant bacteria. However, high-resolution structural studies of phages targeting Pseudomonas aeruginosa-a top-seven global pathogen-particularly podophages, remain severely limited, directly impeding structure-based development of novel antimicrobials. In this study, we utilize cryo-EM to resolve the high-resolution intact structure of mature phage A1002, a podophage infecting carbapenem-resistant P. aeruginosa. Based on density maps combined with AlphaFold3 predictions, we identified 11 structural protein components from the head to
papers.summary: This study uses cryo-EM to determine the high-resolution intact structure of phage A1002, a podophage that infects carbapenem-resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa. The authors identify 11 structural protein components and describe a distinctive tail architecture featuring a split nozzle and two-protein chain-like fibers. This provides a structural template for developing phage-based antimicrobials against a major antibiotic-resistant pathogen.

papers.title: Clonal tree frequency analysis reveals affinity determinants and enables antibody lead optimization.
papers.abstract: Understanding the sequence determinants of antibody affinity within a clonal family is a central challenge in therapeutic antibody discovery. Here, we applied amino acid frequency analysis to a large phylogenetic clonal tree of anti-ST2 monoclonal antibodies, where V(D)J recombination is constant and only somatic hypermutations vary. We identified M33I and L100I in the heavy chain as key affinity-governing mutations, corroborated by AlphaFold2 structural modeling and molecular dynamics free‑energy decomposition. The I33/I100 genotype predicted significantly improved functional neutralization o
papers.summary: The authors analyzed amino acid frequencies across a phylogenetic clonal tree of anti-ST2 antibodies to identify mutations that drive affinity maturation, pinpointing M33I and L100I in the heavy chain as key affinity-governing positions. AlphaFold2 structural modeling and molecular dynamics free-energy decomposition corroborated these findings, and the I33/I100 genotype predicted improved functional neutralization. This demonstrates a clonal-tree frequency approach for antibody lead optimization.

papers.title: Unveiling Molecular Basis of Terminalia chebula in Modulating the AGE-RAGE-PRKCB Axis in Diabetic Nephropathy: Integrative Network Pharmacology and Computational Study.
papers.abstract: AbstractDiabetic nephropathy (DN), a progressive microvascular complication of diabetes, remains a principal cause of renal failure worldwide, yet its multifaceted molecular complexity continues to challenge effective therapeutic intervention. In this study, an integrative network pharmacology and computational modeling framework was employed to unravel the mechanistic basis of Terminalia chebula in mitigating DN pathology. A total of 357 phytoconstituents were retrieved from the IMPPAT 2.0 and PubChem databases and screened through SwissADME and pkCSM, yielding 14 bioactive, drug-like, and no
papers.summary: This study uses network pharmacology and computational modeling to predict how phytochemicals from the medicinal plant Terminalia chebula might act against diabetic nephropathy. Starting from 357 compounds, the authors filtered to 14 drug-like bioactives and mapped them onto the AGE-RAGE-PRKCB signaling axis, suggesting a multi-target mechanism. The work is purely computational and provides hypotheses rather than experimental validation.

papers.title: Expression of Concern: Discovery of ROCK2 inhibitors through computational screening of ZINC database: Integrating pharmacophore modeling, molecular docking, and MD simulations.
papers.summary: This is an Expression of Concern notice for a previously published study that used computational screening of the ZINC database, pharmacophore modeling, molecular docking, and MD simulations to identify ROCK2 inhibitors. The notice does not present new findings; it flags concerns about the integrity or reliability of the published work. Readers should treat the original results with caution pending resolution.

papers.title: Integrated metabolomic, transcriptomic and computational analyses reveal geographical variation and potential anti-osteoarthritis bioactive compounds in Arenga pinnata pith.
papers.abstract: Arenga pinnata pith is an underexplored plant resource whose chemical and transcriptional characteristics may vary substantially among geographical populations. Here, we performed a comparative multi-omics analysis of pith samples collected from Hainan, Jiangxi, and Taiwan in China, as well as Thailand and Indonesia, using untargeted metabolomics and transcriptome sequencing. Metabolomic profiling detected 1,707 metabolite features spanning major classes including amino acids and derivatives, flavonoids, phenolic acids, alkaloids, and lipids. Clear geographical differences were observed in bot
papers.summary: This study combined untargeted metabolomics and transcriptome sequencing to profile Arenga pinnata pith from five geographic regions, detecting 1,707 metabolite features across amino acids, flavonoids, phenolic acids, alkaloids, and lipids. The authors found clear geographic variation in chemical and transcriptional profiles and used computational analyses to identify candidate bioactive compounds with potential anti-osteoarthritis activity. The work highlights an underexplored plant resource and links geography to phytochemical diversity.

papers.title: Identification and expression analysis of intergenic long non-coding RNAs (lincRNA) associated with stripe rust resistance in wheat.
papers.abstract: Long intergenic non-coding RNAs (lincRNAs) have emerged as important regulators of plant immune responses, yet their functional landscape in wheat (Triticum aestivum) during stripe rust (Puccinia striiformis f. sp. tritici) infection remains largely unexplored.
papers.summary: This study identifies and profiles long intergenic non-coding RNAs (lincRNAs) in wheat during infection by the stripe rust fungus, a major pathogen of wheat. The authors characterize lincRNAs associated with resistance responses, providing a first look at this regulatory layer in wheat immunity. The work expands the catalog of non-coding regulatory elements potentially involved in plant disease resistance.

papers.title: Exploring Moringa-Derived Phytosterol From East Nusa Tenggara, Indonesia, as Antialopecia Agent: 5α-Reductase Inhibition and Topical Tonic for Sustainable Health Innovation and Development.
papers.abstract: Alopecia is a continuous hair loss of more than 125 strands per day, with a prevalence of 70% in men and 30% in women in Indonesia. This condition can be attributed to hormonal factors (androgens). Meanwhile, moringa (Moringa oleifera Lamk.) seed oil from East Nusa Tenggara (ENT) Province, Indonesia, contains steroids, fatty acids, and tocopherols. These compounds have demonstrated antiseborrheic activity against Malassezia furfur and antialopecia activity in rabbits induced by dihydrotestosterone (DHT). Therefore, this study aimed to characterize moringa oil, isolate and identify phytosterol
papers.summary: This study characterizes moringa seed oil from East Nusa Tenggara, Indonesia, and isolates phytosterol compounds to evaluate their potential as anti-alopecia agents via 5α-reductase inhibition and topical tonic formulation. The work connects local botanical resources to a sustainable health innovation targeting androgen-driven hair loss.

papers.title: Synthesis, crystal structure, and characterization of a new crystalline berberine-2-sulfobenzoate salt, integrating vibrational spectroscopy and quantum chemical investigation.
papers.abstract: A hydrothermal crystallization screen was conducted to expand the solid-form landscape of berberine. Hydrolysis of saccharin under the applied conditions produced 2-sulfobenzoic acid, leading to the formation of a new crystalline berberine-2-sulfobenzoate salt (BER-SBA). Single-crystal X-ray diffraction established a 1:1 salt structure stabilized by C-H•••O interactions between berberine and sulfobenzoate ions and O-H•••O interactions between neighboring sulfobenzoate units. Agreement between the experimental and simulated powder X-ray diffraction patterns confirmed the phase identity of the b
papers.summary: This paper reports the hydrothermal synthesis and crystal structure of a new berberine-2-sulfobenzoate salt, formed unexpectedly when saccharin hydrolyzed to 2-sulfobenzoic acid under the reaction conditions. Single-crystal X-ray diffraction revealed a 1:1 salt stabilized by C-H···O and O-H···O hydrogen-bonding interactions, and the phase was confirmed by matching experimental and simulated powder diffraction patterns. Vibrational spectroscopy and quantum chemical calculations were used to further characterize the material.

papers.title: Exploring biomarkers and regulatory mechanisms associated with 20 protein post-translational modifications in acute myocardial infarction based on transcriptomics.
papers.abstract: Acute myocardial infarction (AMI) is a critical condition resulting from coronary occlusion, leading to myocardial necrosis and dysfunction. Protein posttranslational modifications (PTMs) regulate key inflammatory and signaling pathways in its pathogenesis. Accordingly, exploring transcriptomic signatures of genes encoding PTM-regulatory factors may provide valuable insights for improving early diagnosis and therapeutic stratification in AMI.
papers.summary: This study uses transcriptomic data to identify genes encoding regulators of 20 different protein post-translational modifications (PTMs) as potential biomarkers for acute myocardial infarction (AMI). The authors aim to link PTM-regulatory gene expression signatures to inflammatory and signaling pathways in AMI pathogenesis, with the goal of improving early diagnosis and therapeutic stratification.

papers.title: Identification of candidate HLA-E binding peptides from Mycobacterium tuberculosis using phage secretome library screening and computational modeling.
papers.abstract: Mycobacterium tuberculosis (Mtb) remains a primary global health challenge, particularly in HIV-co-infected populations where viral Nef-mediated downregulation of classical MHC-I molecules impairs T-cell immunity. Conversely, the non-classical MHC-Ib molecule, HLA-E, is resistant to Nef-mediated evasion, representing an attractive, non-polymorphic pathway for investigating potential Mtb-specific CD8+ T-cell activation targets.
papers.journal: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology
papers.summary: This study identifies candidate Mycobacterium tuberculosis peptides that bind HLA-E, a non-classical MHC-I molecule resistant to HIV Nef-mediated immune evasion, using phage secretome library screening combined with computational modeling. The work highlights HLA-E as a potential non-polymorphic pathway for Mtb-specific CD8+ T-cell activation, particularly relevant in HIV co-infection where classical MHC-I presentation is impaired.

papers.title: Bone morphogenetic protein 4 meets artificial intelligence: a comprehensive review of AI-driven advances in drug discovery, structural modeling, and clinical translation.
papers.abstract: Bone Morphogenetic Protein 4 (BMP4), a member of the transforming growth factor-beta (TGF-β) superfamily, plays pivotal roles in embryonic development, tissue homeostasis, and disease pathogenesis-including cancer, fibrosis, and fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva (FOP). The rapid advancement of artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) methodologies over the past 5 years has created unprecedented opportunities for understanding and therapeutically targeting BMP4 biology at multiple scales, from atomic-resolution structure prediction to population-level clinical prognostication.
papers.summary: This review surveys how AI and machine learning are being applied to BMP4 biology, spanning drug discovery, structural modeling, and clinical translation. It highlights that recent AI methods now enable analysis of BMP4 from atomic-resolution structure prediction up to population-level clinical prognostication, with relevance to cancer, fibrosis, and fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva.

papers.title: Prediction of the binding modes between key differential flavor compounds in tobacco leaves at different maturity stages and the olfactory receptor OR1D2.
papers.abstract: Leaf maturity is a critical determinant of the sensory quality of tobacco. To elucidate the microstructural characteristics of Yunyan 87 tobacco at distinct maturity stages and the perception mechanisms of key differential flavor compounds mediated by the olfactory receptor OR1D2.
papers.summary: This study examines how tobacco leaf maturity affects flavor compound profiles and predicts how key differential volatile compounds bind to the human olfactory receptor OR1D2. It combines flavor chemistry with molecular docking/modeling to link leaf maturity to sensory perception mechanisms.

papers.title: Loop region mutations in Omp33-36: unveiling reduced antimicrobial permeability and resistance in Acinetobacter baumannii through structural modeling and membrane-protein simulations.
papers.abstract: Acinetobacter baumannii can reduce its susceptibility to antimicrobials by altering the permeability of the outer membrane, e.g., by changing the abundance and function of porins. Omp33-36 has been implicated in susceptibility to multiple antibiotics including carbapenems, but the structural effect of sequence variations observed in clinical isolates is poorly understood. We investigated whether substitutions in Omp33-36 from multidrug-resistant clinical isolates affect porin dynamics and contribute to permeability-related resistance.
papers.summary: This study uses structural modeling and membrane-protein simulations to investigate how mutations in the loop regions of the Acinetobacter baumannii porin Omp33-36, observed in multidrug-resistant clinical isolates, affect porin dynamics. The findings suggest these loop substitutions alter porin behavior in ways that reduce outer membrane permeability, contributing to antimicrobial resistance. The work links clinical sequence variation to structural mechanisms of permeability-based resistance in a major nosocomial pathogen.

papers.title: Integrated computational screening and biochemical validation identify natural small molecules targeting Aβ aggregation and dissociation.
papers.abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is characterized by the accumulation of amyloid-β (Aβ), a pathological hallmark implicated in disease onset and progression. Aβ undergoes self-assembly from monomers into soluble oligomers, protofibrils, insoluble fibrils, and extracellular plaques. Our previous studies have shown that Jowiseungchungtang, which consists of 14 medicinal herbs, inhibits Aβ aggregation and ameliorates Aβ-mediated pathology in AD models. However, the active small molecules underlying these effects remain unidentified. To identify small molecules from these 14 medicinal herbs, we constructe
papers.journal: Journal of pharmacy & pharmaceutical sciences : a publication of the Canadian Society for Pharmaceutical Sciences, Societe canadienne des sciences pharmaceutiques
papers.summary: This study combines computational screening with biochemical experiments to identify natural small molecules from a 14-herb traditional medicine formula that can both inhibit amyloid-beta aggregation and dissociate existing aggregates. The work links specific plant-derived compounds to anti-amyloid activity, offering starting points for Alzheimer's disease drug development.

papers.title: Cannabidiol suppresses M2-like macrophage polarization via TRPV4/RhoA/ROCK signaling to alleviate hepatic fibrosis.
papers.abstract: Dysregulated buildup of extracellular matrix constitutes a hallmark of hepatic fibrosis, loss of liver architectural integrity, and impaired hepatic functional capacity. Pro-fibrogenic M2-polarized macrophages promote the transdifferentiation of hepatic stellate cells and facilitate fibrotic progression. Cannabidiol (CBD) exhibits immunomodulatory and anti-fibrotic properties. However, whether CBD regulates M2-like macrophage polarization to mitigate hepatic fibrogenesis remains unclear.
papers.summary: This study investigates whether cannabidiol (CBD) can reduce liver fibrosis by preventing macrophages from adopting a pro-fibrotic M2-like state. The authors propose that CBD acts through TRPV4/RhoA/ROCK signaling to suppress M2 polarization, thereby limiting activation of hepatic stellate cells and extracellular matrix buildup. The work links CBD's immunomodulatory effects to a specific signaling pathway in liver fibrosis.

papers.title: Mechanistic investigation of clarithromycin in ulcerative colitis involving Kv1.3 downregulation and modulation of the Th17/Treg balance.
papers.abstract: Present therapies for ulcerative colitis (UC) frequently encounter challenges due to medication resistance and side effects, underscoring the necessity to discover secure and efficacious therapeutic targets. Clarithromycin (CLA), a macrolide antibiotic, has not been fully characterized with respect to its anti-inflammatory mechanisms and therapeutic potential in UC.
papers.summary: This study investigates whether clarithromycin, a macrolide antibiotic, can alleviate ulcerative colitis by downregulating the potassium channel Kv1.3 and rebalancing Th17 and regulatory T cells. The findings suggest a mechanistic rationale for repurposing clarithromycin as an anti-inflammatory therapy in UC, though the work is preclinical and based on mechanistic exploration rather than clinical trials.

papers.title: The Plant-Derived Peptide Hyde C1 Exhibits Membrane-Associated Antifungal Activity and Protects Against Systemic Candida albicans Infection.
papers.abstract: Invasive candidiasis and increasing antifungal resistance underscore the need for alternative therapeutic approaches. Antimicrobial peptides are of interest because of their antifungal activity and potential membrane-associated effects. This study evaluated Hyde C1, a plant-derived antimicrobial peptide from Cichorium intybus, for antifungal activity against Candida albicans and examined whether its effects were associated with fungal membrane-associated effects.
papers.summary: Hyde C1, a peptide from chicory (Cichorium intybus), shows antifungal activity against Candida albicans that appears to act at the fungal membrane, and it protected against systemic C. albicans infection in a model system. The work positions this plant peptide as a possible alternative or adjunct to conventional antifungals amid rising resistance.

papers.title: Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) and cancer: knowledge mapping and emerging trends based on a bibliometric analysis.
papers.abstract: To systematically map the global publication landscape, collaboration patterns, thematic structure, and emerging research activity in the literature on per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) and cancer.
papers.summary: This bibliometric analysis maps the global research landscape on PFAS and cancer, identifying publication trends, collaboration networks, thematic clusters, and emerging research hotspots. It provides a structured overview of the field rather than new experimental findings, highlighting areas of growing interest and potential gaps.

papers.title: Quercetin attenuates acute inflammation and extracellular matrix remodeling after intracerebral hemorrhage: transcriptomics-informed network pharmacology and experimental validation.
papers.abstract: Intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH) induces secondary brain injury characterized by neuroinflammation, blood-brain barrier disruption, oxidative stress, and extracellular matrix (ECM) remodeling. Quercetin (QR), a natural flavonoid with anti-inflammatory and antioxidant activities, has shown neuroprotective potential; however, the molecular signatures associated with its effects in acute ICH remain incompletely defined. In this study, QR-related target prediction, ICH-associated gene mining, endoplasmic reticulum stress-related gene annotation, and 2 mouse brain transcriptomic datasets were integra
papers.summary: This study combines network pharmacology, transcriptomic data from mouse brain after intracerebral hemorrhage, and experimental validation to show that quercetin reduces acute neuroinflammation and extracellular matrix remodeling. The authors identify candidate molecular targets and pathways through which quercetin may protect the brain following hemorrhage. Experimental work supports the predicted anti-inflammatory and ECM-stabilizing effects.

papers.title: Hupehenine suppresses tumor cell phenotypes and modulates macrophage marker profiles in a diabeticmimetic colorectal cancer model.
papers.abstract: Diabetes is associated with increased colorectal cancer (CRC) risk and mortality, but the molecular links remain incompletely understood. We aimed to characterize shared molecular features of diabetes and CRC, and identify compounds capable of modulating the candidate axis at this interface.
papers.summary: This study identifies shared molecular features between diabetes and colorectal cancer, then tests whether the natural compound hupehenine can modulate these pathways in a diabetic-mimetic CRC model. Hupehenine suppressed tumor cell phenotypes and altered macrophage marker profiles, suggesting it may target the diabetes–cancer interface.

papers.title: Structure-based minimization of a high-mobility group protein B1 (HMGB1) B box peptide uncouples anti-NETotic activity and anti-biofilm function.
papers.abstract: We previously showed that human HMGB1 has anti-biofilm activity localized to a 97-amino-acid B-Box-derived peptide (mB Box-97), engineered with a C106S mutation to reduce HMGB1's proinflammatory properties while retaining anti-biofilm function. This peptide also suppresses NETosis by inhibiting neutrophil protein kinase C (PKC) activity. Here, we tested whether the anti-biofilm and anti-NETotic activities of mB Box-97 could be separated into distinct shorter peptides by constructing truncated variants containing Helix 1 of the B-Box (with the C106S mutation), with or without the A Box-B Box li
papers.summary: The authors truncated the HMGB1 B-box-derived peptide mB Box-97 into shorter variants containing Helix 1 (with the C106S mutation), with or without the A Box–B Box linker, to test whether its anti-biofilm and anti-NETosis activities could be separated. They found that these two functions can be uncoupled into distinct shorter peptides, suggesting that the anti-NETotic (PKC-inhibitory) and anti-biofilm activities are structurally separable. This provides a basis for engineering HMGB1-derived peptides with reduced proinflammatory liability and more selective function.

papers.title: Unleashing the industrial potential of microbial plant cell wall polysaccharide-degrading enzymes: recent advances in protein engineering.
papers.abstract: Plant cell wall polysaccharide-degrading enzymes (PCWPEs) used in industry are predominantly of microbial origin. Key enzyme classes, including cellulases, lytic polysaccharide monooxygenases (LPMOs), β-xylanases, β-mannanases and pectinases, have attained technological maturity and are widely deployed across agro-waste biorefineries, food and feed processing, textile and pulp manufacturing. Low catalytic efficiency, insufficient thermostability, poor operational adaptability, restricted functionality, and product inhibition limit the industrial use of these enzymes. Structure- and sequence-gu
papers.summary: This review examines recent protein engineering advances aimed at improving microbial plant cell wall polysaccharide-degrading enzymes (cellulases, LPMOs, xylanases, mannanases, pectinases) for industrial use. It focuses on overcoming limitations such as low catalytic efficiency, poor thermostability, and product inhibition through structure- and sequence-guided engineering strategies. The paper consolidates progress toward making these enzymes more robust and adaptable for biorefineries, food/feed processing, textiles, and pulp manufacturing.
